SPARK

Jul–Nov 2024

AI conversation across web and mobile

SPARK is a personal AI assistant for web and Android. On the web, users can start with a suggested prompt, type their own question, or return to a saved conversation. I led 12 contributors across web, mobile, backend, machine learning, and data for UNSRAT IT Community (UNITY).

Development lead
Speech service source

Problem

Bring text conversations, saved chat sessions, and voice interaction together across web and Android clients.

My role

Development lead responsible for coordinating delivery across the web, mobile, AI, and data teams and supervising their integration workflows.

Approach

The team connected Next.js and Flutter clients to a NestJS backend with JWT authentication, Socket.IO messaging, and Prisma-backed PostgreSQL chat history.

Voice workflow

On Android, users tap the microphone to start a voice conversation. SPARK transcribes their speech and responds in real time, with speech synthesis for Indonesian replies.

Service integration

Separate gRPC contracts connect the chat backend to AI responses and speech synthesis. Python services use Flask, SpeechRecognition, and Edge TTS for Indonesian speech workflows.

Result

UNITY launched SPARK on 11 November 2024. Our team delivered the web and Android apps, chat backend, and speech service, and demonstrated the assistant at TECHOFEST 2024.
